taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs 10-30 dm, canes ascending, often arching.

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs to 30 dm.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves deciduous.

traits.stem_clump.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems one to several from the crown, biennial; drawn as a clump of canes.

traits.spines.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs armed: prickles moderate to dense on the canes.

traits.spine_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): prickles erect or curved, 4-8 mm, usually broad-based.

traits.bark_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): canes strongly pruinose, glaucous white (whitebark); sRGB by eye.

traits.leaf_colour.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaflets mid green above, white beneath.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves palmately compound or ternate.

traits.division_pattern.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): palmately compound or ternate.

traits.division_order.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets undivided, unlobed or shallowly 3-lobed.

traits.leaflets.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets 3-5 (to 7).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): terminal leaflet 6-10 cm; a palmate blade is about as long as its end leaflet, a little more where its stalk shows.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 8 cm to 16 cm across the leaflets.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): terminal leaflet 6-10 cm long.

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): terminal leaflet 3-6 cm wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): terminal leaflet ovate to lanceolate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflet apex acuminate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflet margins serrate to doubly serrate.

traits.leaf_hairs_beneath.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis var. leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves white-tomentose beneath.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flat-topped cymiform or umbelliform clusters; drawn as a corymb, flat-topped.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis var. leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): (2-)3-10 (to 12) flowers.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: flat clusters 3 cm to 6 cm long.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: open flowers 1 cm to 1.5 cm across, the petals erect then ascending.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals white, 3-6 (to 8) mm.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals white; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits 1-2 cm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits reddish purple to nearly black; drawn near black; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits depressed globose to conic.

traits.fruitlets_per_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis var. leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): drupelets (20-)30-60 to a fruit; var. nigerrimus 20-40.

traits.fruitlet_coherence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): drupelets coherent, the fruit coming away from its torus, so hollow.

traits.fruit_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis var. leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): drupelets pubescent; var. nigerrimus glabrous.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rubus leucodermis var. leucodermis (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowering April to August.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: fruit ripe June to August.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a clump of arching chalk-white canes with hooked prickles, leaves of three to five leaflets white beneath, small white flowers in flat clusters and dark purple-black caps of fruit.

allometry.note: 2.1 m tall at 8 years in the open, inside the floras' range of heights, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
